newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue-chips close strongly; small-caps tumble.
newsitem.headline: KL blue-chips close strongly; small-caps tumble.

text.p: Malaysian blue-chips closed the day on a strong note as foreign institutional investors were seen gradually accumulating them, said analysts and dealers
The benchmark Composite Index closed up 8.40 points at 1,147.72, while the all-share EMAS Index was up 2.13 at 333.10. The Second Board Index closed down 13.40 at 575.44.
Finance firm Hong Leong Credit was up 1.3 ringgit at 13.20 on speculation of a restructuring in the Hong Leong group.
"Hong Leong Credit and Hong Leong Bank have both posted good earnings recently after being laggard stocks, but they probably should not be moving as fast as they are," said an analyst.
"Bank Negara is encouraging banks to merge with one another, but the industry-wide restructuring is not going to take place overnight," he added.

Volumes were high as 284 million shares were traded, valued at 2.33 billion ringgit. Roughly 73 percent of the traded volume was from Main Board stocks. Losers led gainers 337 to 259, with 129 stocks unchanged.
"It seems as if the speculation has moved from the Second Board to the Main Board," said the analyst.
United Engineers was up 20 cents at 19.90 on institutional buying.
